input: Merge email addresses from /data/list1.txt, /data/list2.txt, and /data/list3.txt into a single deduplicated, alphabetically sorted list. Save it to /data/combined.txt and print the total count of unique emails.

transcript.final_response:
I merged the three lists into `/data/combined.txt`, sorted alphabetically with duplicates removed. **There are 6 unique emails.**

```
alice@example.com
bob@example.com
charlie@example.com
dave@example.com
eve@example.com
frank@example.com
```

The three files had 9 entries in total, and 3 were duplicates: bob was in lists 1 and 2, alice in lists 1 and 3, and eve in lists 2 and 3.

The files were already clean. To be safe, the merge also trims spaces, drops blank lines and Windows line endings, and makes everything lowercase so that differently capitalised copies of the same address count as one.
tool_calls: cd /data; for f in list1.txt list2.txt list3.txt; do echo "== $f"; cat -A "$f" | head -50; wc -l "$f"; done

cd /data; cat list1.txt list2.txt list3.txt | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//' | grep -v '^$' | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | sort -u > combined.txt; cat combined.txt; echo "Total unique emails: $(wc -l < combined.txt)"
